title: Best small business insurance in the UK (2026): public liability, employers’ liability and professional cover

sections.content: Small business insurance can protect a company from claims, accidents, property damage, legal costs and disruption. This guide explains the main types of cover UK small businesses should compare, including public liability, employers’ liability, professional indemnity, business contents and cyber cover.

sections.title: 1. What small business insurance usually covers
sections.content: The right cover depends on how the business operates. A shop, tradesperson, consultant, landlord, online seller and local service business may all need different insurance. The most common policies include public liability, employers’ liability, professional indemnity, business equipment cover, stock cover, business interruption cover and cyber insurance.

sections.title: 2. Public liability insurance
sections.content: Public liability insurance is designed for claims from members of the public, customers or clients. It can be important if customers visit your premises, you visit client locations, or your work could cause injury or property damage.

sections.title: 3. Employers’ liability insurance
sections.content: Employers’ liability insurance is usually a legal requirement if you employ staff in the UK. It helps cover claims from employees who become ill or injured because of their work.

sections.title: 4. Professional indemnity insurance
sections.content: Professional indemnity insurance is useful for consultants, advisers, designers, agencies, accountants, IT firms and other businesses that provide professional advice or services. It can help with claims linked to mistakes, negligence, poor advice or missed obligations.

sections.title: 5. How to compare policies
sections.content: Compare more than the headline price. Check the cover limit, excess, exclusions, optional add-ons, claims process, monthly payment cost, cancellation terms and whether the insurer understands your trade or sector.

sections.title: 6. What to prepare before getting quotes
sections.content: Have your business name, trading address, industry, turnover, number of employees, claims history, equipment or stock value, and a clear description of your work. Better information usually helps insurers quote more accurately.

sections.title: Do all small businesses need insurance?
sections.content: Not every policy is legally required, but many businesses need cover because clients, landlords, lenders or contracts ask for it. Employers’ liability is usually required if you employ staff.

sections.title: Should sole traders compare business insurance?
sections.content: Yes. Sole traders may still need public liability, professional indemnity, equipment cover or income-protection-style cover depending on the work they do.
